title: dedicated-capacity-weekly-prep-liam-chen
content:
Weekly prep notes for dedicated capacity sync — focus: GPU pool forecasts, reservation planning, and autoscaling policy tweaks.

Meeting date: 2026-02-26 (weekly sync)
Attendees (planned): Liam Chen (me), Maya Patel, Evan Brooks, Priya Shah (SRE), Tony Vega (sales ops, optional)
Goal: align on next-90-day GPU reservations, confirm autoscale thresholds for N. Virginia pools, surface capacity risks for top 5 customers, and agree on follow-ups for infra tickets.

Current context / tl;dr:
- Q1 reserved usage is at 78% across prod pools; forecasted demand spike from Customer A (fintech) and Customer C (ecommerce) starting mid-March due to new feature rollouts.
- We still have ~18 spare A100s in us-east-1 flexible pool, but these are fragmented across hosts (bad bin-packing).
- Autoscale events last week: 23 scale-ups, 2 failed scale-ups (both transient due to image pull). Need to reduce failure window.

Key metrics (last 7d):
- Avg token qps per pool (prod-east-1): 12.3k
- Median latency (p95 generation): 210ms
- Reserved utilization: 78%
- On-demand allocation count: 42 instances (G4dn/G5)

Forecast assumptions for next 90 days:
- Base growth: +12% M/M from organic usage (conservative)
- Customer A pilot -> production: +250% for their routes starting 2026-03-15 (phased rollout over 2 weeks)
- New customers (pipeline): 2 mid-market deals expected to start in April, estimate addtl +6% consumption if closed
- Risk: higher variance if Customer C moves to 90% traffic share to dedicated pool

Prelim reservation ask (draft numbers, need engineering validation):
- us-east-1: reserve +40 A100-equivalent vGPUs (covers projected peak + buffer)
- eu-west-1: reserve +8 (small uptick expected)
- ap-southeast-1: hold — revisit after May usage review

Autoscaling policy notes / proposed tweaks:
- Currently scale-up threshold: 75% host utilization for 30s. Proposal: increase to 80% for burst-y workloads to reduce churning (sim simulation shows ~6% cost reduction, +2% latency).
- Add backoff for image-pull failures: retry count -> 4 (from 2) with exponential backoff (10s, 20s, 40s). Also pre-warm images on standby hosts to avoid pulls during peak.
- Introduce predictive scaling for scheduled customer deployments (Customer A window). Hook into deployment CI to create temp capacity reservations for 48-72h during rollout.

Operational concerns / open questions:
- Bin-packing: fragmentation causing effective usable capacity loss (~6% inefficiency). Options: rebalancer job during low-traffic windows vs. increased oversubscription. Need SRE input on safe window.
- Cost vs SLA: Reservations reduce unit cost but increase upfront spend; finance needs final numbers before signing. Maya to coordinate.
- Image registry throttling: observed spikes during scale-ups. Is registry rate-limited? Ask infra to confirm.

Agenda for sync (25m):
1) Quick readout of metrics + forecast assumptions (5m)
2) Reservation proposal and finance questions (8m)
3) Autoscale policy adjustments & SRE tradeoffs (7m)
4) Action items + owners (5m)

Action items (immediate):
- [Liam] Finalize forecast spreadsheet with per-customer route-level breakdown and send to Maya + Priya by EOD 2026-02-24. (in progress)
- [Maya] Run reservation cost vs spot/on-demand calc and prepare finance-facing summary for reservations request by 2026-02-28.
- [Evan] Prototype pre-warm image job (k8s cron) and run in staging; report failure modes by 2026-03-03.
- [Priya] Validate proposed autoscale threshold change in a canary pool (2 hosts) and share latency impact metrics by 2026-03-02.
- [SRE] Investigate registry throttling and confirm any rate limits; estimated ETA 2026-02-27. (assigned to Priya for coordination)
- [Liam/Maya] Draft reservation purchase request for procurement review (include buffer rationale) by 2026-03-01.

Notes / talking points for finance and procurement:
- Emphasize that the +40 A100 ask for us-east-1 is to avoid expensive on-demand churn during Customer A rollout. Show scenario A: no reservation -> 30% on-demand usage at peak vs scenario B: reservation -> on-demand <5%.
- Include amortized cost per token and expected ROI horizon (60–90 days) given Customer A committed ARR.

Follow-ups to surface in weekly update email:
- Update on reservation approval status
- Outcome of autoscale canary tests
- Any procurement blockers
- Post-mortem of last week's scale-up failures (root cause + mitigations)

Notes to self (scratch):
- Remember to pull detailed host-level allocation logs (last 30 days) for bin-packing analysis — query: infra.allocations.hosts.daily
- Check with sales on exact Customer A rollout schedule (timezones!)
- Consider metric: "effective_reserved_capacity" = reserved_count - fragmented_unusable_count (use to justify rebalancer)

Raw links / refs:
- Confluence: DED-Capacity-Runbook (linked above)
- JIRA: DEDCAP-78 (reservation pipeline), DEDCAP-105 (autoscale backoff), INFRA-443 (image registry investigation)
- GH PR: infra/pool-rebalancer draft (PR #912)


End of notes. Will iterate after sync and update the reservation numbers based on SRE feedback.
